findings.title: Backend TLS policy's CA certificate is missing
findings.cause: BackendTLSPolicy auth-tls checks the certificate of Service auth against the CA bundle in ConfigMap auth-ca, and ConfigMap auth-ca has keys ca.pem, and the CA bundle must be under key ca.crt, so the reference is invalid and requests a Gateway sends there fail with a 5xx error

evidence.what: BackendTLSPolicy auth-tls names ConfigMap auth-ca as its CA certificate
evidence.command: kubectl get backendtlspolicy auth-tls -n kd-gateway-backend-tls-ca-missing -o jsonpath='{.spec.validation}'

evidence.what: ConfigMap auth-ca has keys ca.pem, and the CA bundle must be under key ca.crt
evidence.command: kubectl get configmap auth-ca -n kd-gateway-backend-tls-ca-missing -o jsonpath='{.data}'

findings.fix: Create ConfigMap auth-ca in namespace kd-gateway-backend-tls-ca-missing with the backend's CA bundle under key ca.crt (kubectl create configmap auth-ca --from-file=ca.crt=ca.pem -n kd-gateway-backend-tls-ca-missing), or point caCertificateRefs at the ConfigMap that holds it.
